# Report a scam call to the FTC

Goal: file a complete report at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ for an unwanted or scam call, with as little effort from the person as possible.

## 1. Gather the details
Ask one short question at a time, and skip anything they already told you. If they paste a voicemail transcript or a screenshot, pull the details from it yourself before asking.

- **What happened**: the voicemail or call script (pasted text is best), or a short summary. Note what it pitched, such as a loan, an IRS or SSA threat, a car warranty, a fake bank or Amazon alert, or a prize.
- **Caller ID number**: the number shown on their phone. Ask for this separately from any callback number, because scammers often show one number and give another.
- **Callback number**: the number the message said to call or text back, if it's different.
- **Company or person named**, if any, such as a company name, an agent name, a website, or an email.
- **Date and time** of the call, with the time zone. Default to now if they don't know.
- **Robocall?** If it was a prerecorded voice, the answer is yes.
- **Money, information shared, and prior dealings**: these can go in one question ("Did you pay or share anything, or deal with them before?"), since the answer is usually a single no. If they paid, get the amount and method (gift card, wire, crypto, card, Zelle). If they gave out an SSN, bank or card details, or a login, point them to https://www.identitytheft.gov after filing.
- **The person's own phone number**: the number that received the call. The FTC form requires it, and it also requires a phone type. Assume cell unless they say it's a landline or VoIP.
- **Name, email, and address are optional.** Tell them they can stay anonymous, and leave these blank unless they want follow-up from the FTC.

Never invent or guess personal details. Only enter what they gave you.

## 2. Fill out the form
Open https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ and start a report.
- Pick the closest category. A loan pitch goes under "Credit, debt, loan." An imposter (government, bank, tech support, family member) goes under "Impersonator." A pure robocall or telemarketing call goes under "Unwanted calls." Pick the closest sub-type and mention it in the summary.
- "Are you filing for someone else?" can default to Yes. Set it to No unless they are reporting for another person.
- Answer how it started (Phone Call), check the robocall box when it applies, and enter the callback and company phone number, the date and time, and the money answers. The time is split into hour and minute fields.
- "Have you done business…" and "Do you have other information…" can share a single radio group. If they do, choose "Yes, other information" when you have a phone number or name for the scammer.
- The form has no field for the caller ID number, so put it in the comments.
- Comments: one plain paragraph on what happened, both numbers (caller ID and callback), and the verbatim script if you have it.
- In "About you," enter only their phone number, phone type, and country, plus any optional fields they chose to share.

## 3. Submit and confirm
- Before you submit, show them a one-screen summary of what goes in and get a yes.
- Submit, and solve any captcha. The confirmation page usually shows no report number, so save a screenshot of it as their record. The FTC also forwards call reports to the Do Not Call Registry.
- Tell them it's filed and include the screenshot. Mention anything you chose on their behalf (category, phone type), that they can block the number, that the Do Not Call Registry is at https://www.donotcall.gov, and that https://www.identitytheft.gov is there if they shared personal information.

## Rules
- Collect only what the form needs. Don't save their phone number or other personal details to memory unless they ask you to.
- Never call back, text, or engage the scam number.
- One report per call. If the same scammer calls again from a new number, file a new report.
